correctness.rationale: OPT equals the closest-pair distance δ: some two agents share a facility, so their distances sum to at least δ, and placing at all reports except one endpoint of a closest pair attains δ. Omission costs d_i. With u_i=δ/d_i the moment is Σu_i^(2−p)/Σu_i², and at least two u_i equal one. For 0<p<2 put v_i=u_i²; x↦x^(1−p/2) is strictly concave. For fixed total of the n−2 unfixed v_i, the numerator is thus maximized by making them equal. The resulting one-variable ratio [2+(n−2)z^(2−p)]/[2+(n−2)z²] has derivative with sign given by 2(2−p)−4z^p−(n−2)pz²; its unique zero gives the displayed root, value and equality condition. The gaps 1,1/z,…,1/z realize equality. For p=2 the numerator is n and the denominator strictly exceeds two; for p>2 it is unbounded as z→0, using the same family, but finite on each profile. Replay: the scalar derivative and gaps above or RESULT.md lines 26–53. The supplied verify.py was inspected, not executed. These are all-metric supremum statements for distinct locations, not risk-sensitive incentive results.

The profile transform is onto: any list of positive distances whose minimum occurs at least twice is realizable. Sort it, put the first two agents at gap equal to the minimum, then append each remaining agent at a gap equal to its listed distance. Nondecreasing gaps make each new agent's left gap its nearest-neighbor distance.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Taking powers of the nearest-neighbor distance list and realizing it on a new line instance suffices; this does not assume that raising all distances to p>1 preserves a metric. The two suprema are the same on the given all-metric domain, with identical attainment after transforming the extremizing profiles.
